profiles.brendan: The champion has built in layers. The original draft supplied Jeanty, Daniels, Hampton, Flowers, McLaurin and Egbuka. The Nabers purchase added a major receiver for future capital; the Dan trade added Kyren, Dowdle and the pick that became Tyson. That October 2025 deal is now the backbone of the feature’s most important tree. Kyren leads the team’s points actually started in 2026. The Tuten deal recycled Dowdle and waiver addition Golden into a different young back and Jacob’s first. London is the latest completed purchase, at the cost of Warren and two future picks. The current 5–4 head-to-head record is a reminder that a good roster still has to turn scoring into wins. The pending Javonte deal continues the same present-focused direction. This is a title defense funded by a mix of original selections, traded picks, and opportunistic pickups.
profiles.jacob: No owner has appeared in more completed CTE trades. Jacob has built around original selections Gibbs, Allen and McBride while repeatedly changing the supporting roster. The first recorded trade brought Chase Brown. A later purchase brought Lamb, who has supplied 201.80 points in Jacob’s starting lineups this season. The Wilson-to-London-to-Warren sequence shows that even major acquisitions can become intermediate stops. Jacob’s 85–14 all-play record and league-leading scoring make the production case for his current team; the 2025 championship loss remains the unfinished part of the story. The cost is visible in the pick cupboard: only his own second remains for 2027 at this cutoff. Later picks acquired in recent deals soften the longer-term picture, but they do not recreate next year’s first. This is a strong team whose aggressive construction can be measured, rather than merely advertised.
profiles.brett: Brett offers the league’s clearest example of roster continuity: 15 startup selections remain on the current roster. Jefferson, McConkey, Hall, Cook, Walker, Swift, Olave and Herbert still anchor the franchise’s identity. Only one completed trade appears in his history, sending Mike Evans and a 2027 second to Isaiah for Kyle Pitts. His 2025 team made the playoffs but lost to Brendan in the opening round and finished sixth. This season’s 5–4 matchup record is stronger than the 4–5 median record, while the 55–44 all-play record remains positive. Walker, Swift and Cook lead his points actually started through Week 9. Brett has maintained a substantial core without draining his future inventory. The unresolved question is whether continuity can produce a higher finish than last year, rather than whether he has made enough transactions to look busy.
profiles.mike: Mike’s history contains six completed trades, including two that helped build Jacob’s present contender: Chase Brown left in the inaugural deal, and Lamb left in November 2025. The returns included players and future capital, so the present standings alone cannot settle those exchanges. They do show that the scoring recovery has not arrived: Mike is 1–8 head-to-head, 0–9 against the median, and last in current points for. Javonte, acquired in that first trade, leads his points actually started this year. Only four startup selections remain. Mike’s forward inventory is more substantial than his record: six picks in 2027 and eight in 2028, including Jacob’s 2028 first. The proposed Javonte sale would add Jacob’s 2027 first and Antonio Williams. That would deepen an identifiable rebuilding direction, but future picks still need to become useful selections or successful trades.
profiles.carter: Carter inherited Tyler’s franchise and rapidly transformed it. Only Chuba Hubbard and the Denver defense from that franchise’s startup selections appear on today’s roster; that is franchise continuity, not a claim that Carter made the startup picks. All eight completed trades involving this franchise occurred in the 2026 league record under Carter. London became Wilson plus a fourth; that fourth helped acquire Mahomes. Stevenson helped move the first-round selection from 1.05 to 1.03, where Carter chose Price. Price later joined Nix and Washington in the November package with Jacob. Those sequences reveal a manager repeatedly changing the shape of the roster. The present result is 7–11 combined and 36–63 in all-play. Activity has created a very different team, but the results have yet to demonstrate a competitive breakthrough. Carter’s eventual story depends on what this new core produces and what remains after the next deal.
profiles.dan: Dan is central to the league’s trade trees despite participating in only four completed deals. His 2025 exchange with Brendan sent out Kyren and the first that became Tyson, while bringing Skattebo, Tucker and the second that became Antonio. His Wilson trade with Jacob brought Fannin, Shaheed and Jacob’s first. The first later left in the Tuten transaction, which returned Dowdle to the roster where he was originally drafted. This is why counting retained startup players cannot be confused with uninterrupted ownership. Bijan leads Dan’s points actually started this year, but the team is 2–7 head-to-head and 4–5 against the median. The 0.70-point loss to Isaiah captures some of the frustration without explaining away all the results. The pending Antonio-for-Mitchell exchange is a narrower player preference within a larger three-team agreement. Dan’s completed history has redistributed important assets across several contenders.
profiles.isaiah: Isaiah’s personal record begins in Week 4 of 2025, after Jeremy’s first three weeks. The inherited franchise’s startup draft included Chase; describing him as Isaiah’s own draft selection would rewrite the history. The current team has taken a major competitive step: 8–1 against opponents and 6–3 against the median. Its 59–40 all-play record supports a winning season while showing that the head-to-head pace has also benefited from favorable weekly opposition. Isaiah’s two completed trades have reshaped the lineup substantially. Evans arrived for Pitts with a future second coming back, then the brother-to-brother deal sent Chase, Metcalf and Harvey to Elijah for Lamar, Amon-Ra, Marks and a future third. Six 2027 selections remain under Isaiah’s control. This is both a contender in the current results and a franchise with extra near-term draft capital, rather than an all-in roster stripped of future options.
profiles.cotton: Cotton’s two completed trades both occurred in 2025. Nabers went to Brendan for a first and a third; the first became Denzel Boston at 1.12. Shaheed went to Jacob for Keenan Allen and two fourths; one fourth became Drew Allar, who was later dropped. Those branches should be evaluated separately: a draft pick becoming a player does not mean that player stayed or produced a return. Ten startup selections remain, including Henry, McCaffrey, Jameson Williams, Hockenson and Odunze. The 2026 rookie draft also supplied Mendoza, Sarratt and Branch. Current results remain difficult at 4–14 combined, with a 1–8 median record and 28–71 all-play record. Six picks in 2027 give Cotton options. The franchise is carrying both a veteran scoring core and developing assets, but neither category has yet translated into the sustained weekly production needed to climb.
profiles.jerry: Jerry’s two regular seasons form the strongest sustained results argument in CTE. He led the inaugural combined standings at 25–3 and is tied at 16–2 now. That still has not produced a title: Brendan eliminated him in the 2025 semifinal, after which Jerry won the third-place game. Only one completed trade appears in Jerry’s ledger, the Daniel Jones sale for Brendan’s fourth and a future second. Much of the current success therefore traces to his original selections and waiver work. Smith-Njigba leads the team’s points actually started through Week 9; Watson, acquired in October 2025, is second. Nine startup selections remain, including Bowers, Achane, Pickens and Maye. Jerry is undefeated against the median this season, but the inaugural playoffs already demonstrated the limit of that accomplishment. His next milestone is converting regular-season strength into the championship he has not yet won.
profiles.jesse: Jesse is the only franchise with no completed trades in this ledger. Fourteen startup selections remain, including Barkley, Burrow, A.J. Brown, Kittle, Pollard and Waddle. The first rookie selection added Jeremiyah Love, and all four of Jesse’s own picks remain in each of 2027, 2028 and 2029. That untouched draft inventory creates options without assuming he should sell any particular player. The results have improved from 6–22 combined in 2025 to 7–11 through nine weeks this year, although the 33–66 all-play record shows the scoring still trails most of the league. Week 8’s 171.18–133.38 victory over Troy is an important counterpoint to the 124.20-point loss to Jacob three weeks earlier: this team has produced both a statement win and the archive’s biggest defeat. Jesse’s future direction remains unusually open because so little draft capital has been committed elsewhere.
profiles.elijah: Elijah reached the inaugural semifinals, then finished fourth. His current 5–13 combined record is a significant step back, with a 2–7 matchup record and 3–6 against the median. The archive contains two especially close games worth remembering: he beat Jacob by 0.60 in 2025 and lost to Brett by 0.82 in 2026 Week 9. His two completed trades show a willingness to invest in the roster. A 2026 first went to Carter for Brian Thomas Jr.; Carter used that selection on KC Concepcion at 1.09. Then Elijah exchanged Lamar, Amon-Ra, Marks and a future third for Chase, Metcalf and Harvey. Six startup selections remain, including Adams, Montgomery and Love. The new roster’s results are still developing, so the brothers’ deal cannot responsibly be declared settled after one completed week of post-trade scoring. Elijah has changed the personnel behind the comeback attempt; the standings now need to follow.
profiles.troy: Troy’s 2025 split deserves more attention than his fifth-place finish: 6–8 against opponents, but 11–3 against the median. The combined standings preserved the value of a good scoring season despite unfavorable head-to-head results. This year the two records align at 6–3 apiece, producing 12–6 combined and the current lead over Brendan in their division. Twelve startup selections remain, with Puka, Taylor, Higgins and Hurts still defining the team. Puka, Higgins and Taylor lead his points actually started through Week 9. Troy’s only completed trade sent Shakir, Strange and a 2027 third to Dan for Cousins. The move changed a small part of a largely retained core. The competitive question is whether that continuity can take him beyond last year’s opening-round defeat to Elijah. His current 65–34 all-play record provides a stronger foundation than the frustration of last season’s matchup record suggested.

tradeNotes: The first completed trade. Brown remains with Jacob; Moore and Javonte are with Mike at the cutoff. Javonte’s history includes a September 2026 drop and same-day reacquisition, so his custody was not uninterrupted.
Nabers remains with Brendan and has supplied 129.80 points in his 2026 starting lineups. The first became Denzel Boston at 1.12 for Cotton; the 2027 third remains a future asset.
The central fork: Dan’s first became Jordyn Tyson; Brendan’s second became Antonio Williams. Dowdle later returned to Dan in T17. The pending three-team deal would reunite two downstream branches.
Shaheed moved onward to Dan in T07. Jacob’s 2026 fourth became Drew Allar for Cotton, who later dropped him. The future fourth remains with Cotton.

Jones later left Brendan through a drop. The 2026 fourth became CJ Daniels for Jerry; Daniels later left Jerry as well. Those release events prevent an artificial continuous trade chain. Jerry still holds the 2027 second.

Lamb has supplied 201.80 points in Jacob’s submitted 2026 lineups. Mike still holds the acquired players and Jacob’s 2028 first at this cutoff; that future selection’s slot and eventual result are unresolved.
The Wilson transaction divides into two major branches: Wilson moves to Carter in T10, and Jacob’s first moves to Brendan in T17. Shaheed’s input traces directly to T04.
Elijah acquired Thomas; Carter used Elijah’s original first on KC Concepcion at 1.09. Both player endpoints are on those teams’ current rosters.

Henderson remains with Jacob. Carter’s original second became Nicholas Singleton at 2.05 for Jacob. Jacobs, Michael Wilson and Gadsden formed the other side of the package; use their timelines to distinguish current retention from later departures.
London reached Brendan in T21. The fourth went from Carter to Mike in T11. Wilson remains with Carter. These are separate outputs of a package, not one-for-one valuations.
Mahomes remains with Carter. Carter’s 2026 third became Michael Trigg at 3.05 for Mike. The future second and Jacob-origin fourth remain with Mike.
Jacob’s 2028 third traveled from Carter to Mike in T16. Blue’s subsequent history includes a drop, so no later acquisition is automatically a continuation of this trade.
The confirmed draft swap moved Carter from 1.05 to 1.03: Price to Carter, Tate to Mike. Price later went to Jacob in T20; Stevenson remains with Mike.
Two notable branches: Washington went to Carter in T16 before returning to Jacob in T20; Smith went to Carter in T20. Claiborne was Jacob’s own 2026 3.11 selection; Bell was Mike’s 3.03.
Evans and Brett’s 2027 second went to Isaiah; Pitts went to Brett. Both players remain with their receiving franchises, and the second remains with Isaiah.
Washington moved again in T20. Jacob’s 2028 third arrived via T12. Mike retains Worthy, Sutton and both future picks at this cutoff.
Dowdle returned to Dan after T03. Golden reached Brendan through waivers after Elijah dropped him. Jacob’s first arrived from T07 and is now part of the announced pending agreement.
Troy acquired Cousins for two players and a third. The three player endpoints remain on the receiving rosters at this cutoff; the future third is with Dan.
The brothers exchanged six players and a future third. Every traded player remains on the receiving roster at this cutoff. This is a recent, still-developing result, not a finished long-term verdict.
Price traces to the first-round swap in T13. Smith traces to T14. Washington completes his three-trade round trip via T14 and T16. The 2029 picks remain unassigned to exact slots.
London’s direct prior acquisition was T10. Warren was Brendan’s startup selection. This completed deal changes both rosters, but it is too recent for a meaningful post-trade performance verdict.
